narration: In 1933, America did something almost unimaginable. It closed every bank in the country.
Years of bank failures had shattered confidence. Americans rushed to withdraw their savings, and even sound banks struggled to meet the demand.
Less than forty-eight hours after taking office, Franklin Roosevelt suspended banking transactions across the nation.
The government began examining banks and reopening the institutions it considered strong enough to survive.
When banks reopened, the panic began to reverse. Americans started returning money to the banking system instead of pulling it out.
Roosevelt had not simply reopened the banks. He had helped restore the thing the financial system needed most: trust.
